children: will be announcing earnings results this Monday before the bell. Here’s what investors should know.

Lincoln Educational beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $142.6 million, up 22.4% year on year. It was a strong quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates and a solid beat of analysts’ EBITDA estimates. It reported 18,904 enrolled students, up 31.7% year on year.
Is Lincoln Educational a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Lincoln Educational’s revenue to grow 7.4% year on year, slowing from the 23.6% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Lincoln Educational has a history of exceeding Wall Street’s expectations.

Looking at Lincoln Educational’s peers in the consumer discretionary - education services segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Covista delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 10.7%, beating analysts’ expectations by 4.5%, and Laureate Education reported revenues up 21.2%, topping estimates by 0.7%. Covista traded down 3.4% following the results while Laureate Education was also down 8.6%.

There has been positive sentiment among investors in the consumer discretionary - education services segment, with share prices up 4.7% on average over the last month. Lincoln Educational is down 24.9% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $47.40 (compared to the current share price of $17.65).
